defects.failingInput: readLocalDiagnostics/handler with 512-char CJK instanceId+buildId and 14 records of 1000-char codes
defects.red: serialized body was 18176 bytes against the stated 16384-byte cap (the review measured 18119; identity was not in the budget and codes were sliced by UTF-16 units)
defects.fix: the WHOLE body (identity + envelope + records + cursor reserve) is serialized and measured in UTF-8 BYTES; records shrink/pop until the body fits; identity is byte-capped at 256 bytes each and code labels at 512 bytes via code-point-safe truncation; bounds.maxIdentityBytes/maxCodeBytes are published
defects.test: S15c Defect A (asserts Buffer.byteLength(body) <= MAX_DIAGNOSTICS_RESPONSE_BYTES, recordCount > 0, identity <= 256 bytes)

defects.failingInput: handler with no source plus cursor=zzz
defects.red: 400 diagnostics_cursor_invalid instead of the disabled state
defects.fix: disabled is answered BEFORE any limit/cursor validation; an invalid cursor with a source still answers 400
defects.test: S15c Defect B (disabled 200 + invalid-cursor-with-source 400 in one case)

defects.failingInput: oldest-first records without lastRecordAtMs, newest 1 s old
defects.red: state stale with ageMs 400000 (fallback used all[0])
defects.fix: lastRecordAtMs is authoritative when supplied; otherwise the newest record is max(atMs); order-independent
defects.test: S15c Defect C (staleness {stale:false, ageMs:1000}, state ok)

defects.red: conditions was undefined, so loss was only reachable behind the stale state
defects.fix: body.conditions {stale, dropped} always reports both independently; state precedence (disabled > stale > dropped > empty > ok) and the LocalDiagnosticsSource ordering contract are documented in the module
defects.test: S15c Defect D (state stale, loss {dropped:7}, conditions {stale:true,dropped:true})

defects.failingInput: production composition root never passes readDiagnosticsSource
defects.red: not a test failure - a review finding: the route always answers disabled outside tests
defects.fix: recorded explicitly as a DEFERRED WIRE in the module doc and in evidence/other/s15a-tdd.json: the writer (what is recorded, retention, loss accounting) is R20's module-health/Cause boundary; no writer is fabricated here

minors.test: S15c 'a cursor past the end reads as empty, not ok' (API-produced cursor reused against a shrunk source)

minors.red: the generic operator gate's 401 lacked no-store/nosniff on the diagnostics path
minors.fix: the diagnostics route is dispatched BEFORE the generic operator gate, so the handler owns every status (200/400/401/403) and all carry cache-control: no-store + x-content-type-options: nosniff and no CORS headers; the handler authorizes through the same authorizeOperatorRequest
minors.test: S15c 'the diagnostics 401 carries the path headers' (handler-level; route wiring is typechecked and code-reviewed, not socket-tested by design)

messages: expected 18176 to be less than or equal to 16384
expected { ruleMs: 300000, ageMs: 400000 } to match { stale: false, ageMs: 1000 }
expected undefined to deeply equal { stale: true, dropped: true }

regression.note: includes the 6 pre-existing operator auth/readback suites after the gate extraction and the diagnostics route move

designLimits: The record WRITER stays deferred to R20: this module reads an injected source and reports disabled otherwise. Fabricating a writer here would invent retention/loss semantics R20 owns.

The byte caps for identity (256 bytes) and code labels (512 bytes) are formatting limits chosen in this slice and published in body.bounds; calibrating them against real collectors is R20's enablement decision.
The cursor is opaque (base64url decimal offset); the past-end test reuses an API-produced cursor against a shrunk source rather than forging the encoding.
No live socket proof by instruction: the route is typechecked and handler-tested directly; the route's CORS skip and 401 header behaviour are code-reviewed.
